chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Every fast can be separated (broken into parts) except for the three days [of expiation] regarding an oath.
ai.seo_question: Can the three days of fasting for expiating an oath be done non-consecutively?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies that the three-day fast required for expiating an oath (kaffarat al-yamin) does not need to be observed consecutively, allowing for flexibility in its performance. This ruling aligns with the Shia juristic view that distinguishes this specific expiation from others requiring continuous fasting, emphasizing ease for the believer. The narration underscores the practical application of Quranic injunctions regarding oaths, ensuring that the obligation remains manageable while maintaining spiritual discipline.
